name: Modifying an Array (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that increments all elements of the array by 1.

comments.content: We initialize the array of type int to hold the specified numbers. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }.

We want to iterate over the array and increment each element in the array by 1. To really change the array as we march across it, we need to use indexes so we can assign an updated value to each position as we go. We need the array indexes to start at 0 (array indexes start from 0) with every integer number up to but not including the array length.

Note that we cannot try changing array elements with for-each statement "for (x : lst)" that assigns the name x to each of the items in the array in turn, from left to right. Because updating variable x does not update the array where variable x originally came from; in this case, variable x is a piece of memory separate from the array.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than the number of the elements in the array and terminates when the control variable reaches the array length. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.
We can get the number of elements in the array by using the lst.length expression.

Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop. Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.
This statement increments the element at the index i of the array by 1.

The += operator adds 1 to the value of the index i in the array and the result is stored back into the index i of the array. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement lst[i] = lst[i] + 1.

To print the array elements, we need to traverse the array and then print each element as we visit it. We traverse the array elements using for–each statement. This for loop assigns the name x to each of the elements in the array in turn, from left to right, and the print statement will be executed for each.
This statement prints the element that we visited in the array followed by a space character.

Note that we don't use println because it adds an end-of-line character to terminate the output line. We want to print all the elements of the array in the same line; therefore, we use the print method.
